headline: NVIDIA’s TensorRT Model Connect treats coding agents as an engineering system, not a code generator

verified_story_context.summary: NVIDIA describes TensorRT Model Connect as an open-source collection of C++ model reference implementations designed around coding-agent workflows. Its account emphasizes parallel work, model-family isolation, reversible changes, and GPU-backed validation as engineering patterns for letting agents contribute without collapsing project structure or verification.
verified_story_context.why_it_matters: Agentic coding becomes more reliable when repositories are organized for bounded parallelism, changes can be reversed cleanly, and hardware-backed validation is part of the normal loop.

visual.layout: mechanism-rich textbook systems diagram with parallel lanes converging through validation gates
visual.mechanism: Parallel coding-agent work enters isolated model-family lanes, creates reversible changes at explicit checkpoints, passes GPU-backed validation and repository-level integration checks, then converges into one integrated repository.
visual.alt_text: Professional textbook systems diagram showing multiple parallel coding agents working in isolated model-family lanes, creating reversible changes, passing GPU-backed validation and repository integration checks, and converging into an integrated repository.
visual.style: professional high-detail white-background textbook/editorial systems diagram; mechanism-first; crisp technical architecture; no people, humanoid robots, cinematic scenes, decorative objects, stock-photo look, sparse generic cards, dashboards, or overlapping text
required_elements: multiple clearly separated parallel coding-agent work lanes
isolated model-family lanes with visible boundaries
reversible change or commit checkpoints on each lane
clear convergence into one integrated repository
visual.text_policy: Use only short legible mechanism labels. Prefer labels such as Coding agents, Model-family lanes, Reversible changes, GPU validation, Integration checks, Integrated repository. No headline prose or promotional copy.
